citation_convention: pN = 1-based PDF page index. For PDF pages 1-27 the printed page number equals the PDF index. PDF pages 28-29 = 'Addendum-Page 1-2', 30-31 = 'Pack Materials-Page 1-2', 32-38 = package drawings DBV0005A/DRG0008B (unnumbered), 39 = legal notice. value_types: TYP = typical table value at 25 C; MIN/MAX = guaranteed limits (25 C unless 'over temperature' = -40 to +85 C); CURVE = read from a typical-characteristic plot (coordinates taken from the PDF vector paths with axis calibration checked against the printed grid lines, plus visual check of a 300-dpi render); SIM = plot or value labelled as simulation in the datasheet; CALC = value the datasheet obtains from a formula or calculator; DERIVED = computed here from datasheet numbers, not printed in the datasheet.
input_type: JFET input stage (p1 Description; p14 Sec. 7.1), built on TI's proprietary high-voltage, high-speed complementary bipolar SiGe process (p14)

min_stable_gain.conditions: conventional noninverting/inverting gain circuits (Fig. 7-1/7-2); in noise gain 7 V/V the device has 790 MHz SSBW with approximately 50 deg phase margin (p16 Sec. 7.3.3)
min_stable_gain.below_minimum: p1: 'Though typically stable in gains >= 7V/V, the OPA818 is designed for use in applications with lower gains by applying noise-gain shaping techniques.' p15: the second A_OL pole occurs before |A_OL| drops below 0 dB, so phase change > 180 deg at 0 dB and the amplifier cannot be stable at 1 V/V. p16: in a TIA a unity-gain-stable amplifier is not required; at high frequencies the TIA noise gain is set by (C_TOT)/(C_F) ratio, which is greater than 1. Sec. 8.2.2 (p22): G = 2 V/V realised with 10 ohm + 10 pF between the inputs and 3.3 pF across the 301 ohm RF (RG = 301 ohm) gives ~51 deg phase margin; 1-2 pF parasitic capacitance on the inverting input requires retuning; 'A 45 deg phase margin is generally acceptable, but anything less than 40 deg is not recommended'.

supply.dual_or_single: both; split, single, balanced and unbalanced bipolar supplies supported (p23 Sec. 8.3)
supply.recommended: Recommended operating conditions VS = 6 V min, 10 V nom, 13 V max (p4 Sec. 6.3); EC single-supply operating range 6/10/13 V (p6). Sec. 8.3 text (p23) states 'supplies from 6 V (+4/-2 V) to 12 V (+-6 V)'; comparison table (p2) lists VS = +-6.5 V. Split supply with ground midpoint valid for symmetric supplies >= +-4 V; below that use e.g. +4/-2 V because ground is outside the input common-mode range (p17 Sec. 7.4.1).

current_noise.how_measured_or_defined: Simulation (plot label). The plot is labelled 'Common-mode noise'; the datasheet gives no further definition and no physical explanation of the rise. p21: the TINA-TI model 'closely models the voltage and current noise performance of the amplifier'. The datasheet does not say whether this i_n includes or excludes the en x 2 pi f x C_in term that a TIA noise calculation adds separately.
current_noise.derived_check: DERIVED: an en-on-capacitance origin i_n = en x 2 pi f x C with en = 2.2 nV/rtHz would need C = 10.3 pF at 1 MHz, 4.3 pF at 10 MHz and 1.85 pF at 100 MHz, i.e. not a fixed capacitance and much larger than the 2.4 pF input capacitance below ~20 MHz; the simulated i_n is therefore not simply en acting on C_CM + C_DIFF.

input_capacitance.definition_notes: EC table p5: 'Common-mode input impedance 500 || 1.9 GOhm || pF' and 'Differential input impedance 500 || 0.5 GOhm || pF'. p1: 'low 2.4pF total input capacitance'; p16 Sec. 7.3.4: '2.4 pF combined common-mode and differential'. Fig. 8-3 (p20) draws C_DIFF = 0.5 pF and C_CM = 1.9 pF both from the inverting node to ground and sums C_TOT = C_D + C_DIFF + C_CM; the TINA-TI model already contains C_CM and C_DIFF (p21). Sec. 8.1.2 (p19): C_TOT includes photodiode, amplifier common-mode and differential input capacitance and PCB parasitics.

pinout_notes: FB pin (DRG only) is internally connected to VOUT by on-chip metal; 'Internal feedback trace resistance' 0.8/1.2/1.7 ohm min/typ/max (DRG, device off); FB continuous current <= 13 mA abs max (p4, p5, p15 Sec. 7.3.2, Fig. 7-4). PD pin (DRG only): internal 1 Mohm pull-up lets the pin float (enabled). NC pin 6 has no internal connection. CONTRADICTION: pin table p3 says 'Power down (low = enable, high = disable)', whereas the EC table p6 says power on when PD > VTH_EN (>= VS+ - 1 V) and power down when PD < VTH_DIS (<= VS+ - 3 V), and Fig. 8-9 says 'Connect PD to VS+ to enable the amplifier'.

tia_content.what: front-page plot 'Photodiode Capacitance vs 3dB Bandwidth' (closed-loop f-3dB vs C_D for four R_F)
tia_content.measured_or_simulated: not stated. DERIVED check: every value equals Eq. 1 with GBWP = 2.7 GHz and C_TOT = C_D + 2.4 pF (no PCB parasitic) to within 0.2 %, so the plot is a calculation, not a measurement.
tia_content.figure_or_section: p1 front-page figure; p1 Description: 'over 85MHz signal bandwidth in a TIA configuration with 20kOhm TIA gain (RF) and 0.5pF photodiode capacitance (CD)'

tia_content.what: Butterworth TIA bandwidth design equation, Eq. 1: f-3dB = sqrt(GBWP / (2 pi R_F C_TOT)); C_TOT = photodiode + amplifier common-mode and differential capacitance + PCB parasitic; R_F and C_TOT form a noise-gain zero at 1/(2 pi R_F C_TOT) that causes instability unless compensated by C_F (pole); refers to 'Transimpedance Considerations for High-Speed Amplifiers' app report and its Excel calculator
100 kohm high-sensitivity TIA design example (Fig. 8-3, Tables 8-1, 8-2), +-5 V
tia_content.C_F: 0.092 pF (calculator, Q = 0.707, ~65 deg PM, 4.3 % overshoot), realised as a capacitive tee C1 = C2 = 2.2 pF with C_T = 47 pF to ground (Eq. 2: C_EQ = C1 C2/(C1 + C2 + C_T))
tia_content.C_D_or_source_C: C_D = 5 pF; C_TOT = C_D + C_DIFF 0.5 pF + C_CM 1.9 pF = 7.4 pF
tia_content.bandwidth: target 24 MHz; calculator requires GBWP = 2678.14 MHz; TINA-TI simulated f-3dB = 24.6 MHz with ~0.1 dB peaking (Fig. 8-4; vector reading: 100.1 dBOhm flat, 97.0 dBOhm at 24.6 MHz)
tia_content.noise: Fig. 8-5 simulated: flat-band output noise 41 nV/rtHz = 0.41 pA/rtHz input-referred (RF thermal noise 40.7 nV/rtHz at 27 C); output noise (CURVE) 45 nV/rtHz @1 MHz, 68 @3 MHz, 156 @10 MHz, 211 @15 MHz, peak ~245 nV/rtHz (~2.45 pA/rtHz input-referred) at ~22 MHz, 223 @30 MHz, 143 @50 MHz, 78 @90 MHz. Text: mid-frequency en x C_TOT noise dominates the integrated noise; hence use a low-en amplifier.

tia_content.what: TIA operation and output-swing guidance: photodiode reverse biased so photocurrent flows into the feedback loop and the output falls below V_REF with increasing current; V_REF can be biased closer to VS+ for more output swing, within the input common-mode range

front-page application figure 'High-Speed Optical Front-End': OPA818 TIA (R_F = 100 kohm with C_F, +-5 V, V_BIAS photodiode, V_REF1 on IN+) driving a THS4541 fully-differential amplifier into an ADC (V_REF2, V_CM); dynamic-range details referenced to the 'Maximizing the dynamic range of analog TIA front-end' note
small feedback capacitors: if the required C_F is less than 0.15 pF, consider two series resistors each of half the R_F value to reduce the resistor's parasitic capacitance

APD/photodiode layout: place photodiode on the same PCB side as the amplifier; trace inductance between photodiode and feedback network isolates the photodiode capacitance from the noise gain (Eq. 4 noise gain = 1 + Z_F/Z_IN) and reduces phase margin; add R_ISO = 10-20 ohm as close as possible to IN-; close the R_F/C_F/R_ISO loop near the APD pins; cut TO-can leads short or edge-mount the photodiode

general TIA statements: 'Transimpedance gains of 50 kOhm or greater benefit from the low-current-noise JFET input'; TIA noise gain is 1 V/V at low frequency and C_TOT/C_F-set at high frequency (> 1), so a unity-gain-stable amplifier is not required

application_guidance: Layout (p23-p24 Sec. 8.4.1): remove ground/power planes under and around signal I/O pins; decoupling within 0.25 in using 100 pF-0.1 uF C0G/NPO with voltage rating >= 3x supply, plus 2.2-6.8 uF further away; surface-mount resistors, place RF and series output resistor close to IN- and OUT; keep RF + RG load in mind; for noninverting gain keep RF || RG < 50 ohm (p18); thermal pad to a heat-spreading plane with many vias; do not socket. Thermal (p24 Sec. 8.4.1.1): do not exceed TJ = 105 C; worst-case example PD = 10 V x 27.7 mA + 5^2/(4 x (100 || 350.9 ohm)) = 357 mW gives TJ = 104.5 C at TA = 85 C in DRG (54.6 C/W). Single supply (p17, p23): bias inputs and outputs to mid-supply via V_REF; 12 V single supply gives slightly better ac performance and removes -PSRR dc errors. Test circuit Fig. 8-1 (p18): G = +7, RF = 301 ohm, RG = 49.9 ohm, 49.9 ohm output series and input shunt resistors; effective output load 78 ohm.
abs_max_and_input_protection: Abs max (p4 Sec. 6.1): VS 13.5 V; differential input voltage +-5 V; VCM from VS- - 0.5 V to VS- + 10 V; VO VS- - 0.5 V to VS+ + 0.5 V; continuous input current +-10 mA; continuous output current 25 mA; FB pin 13 mA; TJ 125 C; TA -40 to 85 C; Tstg -65 to 150 C. ESD (p4 Sec. 6.2): HBM +-2500 V, CDM +-1000 V. Input protection (p14-p15 Sec. 7.3.1, Fig. 7-3): ESD diodes from every pin to both rails; they typically support 10 mA continuous current; add series resistors on both inputs where higher currents are possible (e.g. +-12 V systems driving the OPA818), keeping them small for noise/bandwidth; there are no back-to-back diodes between IN+ and IN-, so the differential voltage is absorbed by the VGS of the JFET pair - stay within the +-5 V rating.
other_notes: Power-down (DRG only, p6): VTH_EN >= VS+ - 1 V (min), VTH_DIS <= VS+ - 3 V (max); PD pin bias current -3 min / -2 typ uA at PD = VS+, 13 typ / 20 max uA at PD = VS-; turn-on delay 125 ns, turn-off 170 ns; power-down IQ 27 uA typ / 40 uA max.

Device comparison table (p2): OPA818 +-6.5 V, 2700 MHz, FET, 1400 V/us, 2.2 nV/rtHz, min stable gain 7; OPA657 +-5 V, 1600 MHz, 4.8 nV, G >= 7; OPA656 230 MHz unity-gain; OPA659 350 MHz; LMH6629 800/4000 MHz BJT 0.69 nV, G >= 4 or 10 (pin-selectable compensation); OPA858 5500 MHz CMOS 2.5 nV, G >= 7; THS4631 210 MHz.

Gain-of-2 noise-gain-shaped example (p22 Sec. 8.2.2, Fig. 8-6/8-7/8-8): (a) G = 2: RG = 301 ohm, RF = 301 ohm || 3.3 pF, 10 ohm + 10 pF between IN+ and IN-, 100 ohm load, ~51 deg PM, flat response beyond 100 MHz; (b) G = 7: RG = 49.9 ohm, RF = 301 ohm. Fig. 8-8 output noise density (CURVE): G = 2: 5.4 nV/rtHz to ~30 MHz, 7.7 @100 MHz, 10.4 @200 MHz, 12.6 @400 MHz; G = 7: 16.5 nV/rtHz flat, 16.9 @100 MHz, 18.2 @200 MHz, ~20.7 peak near 400 MHz. Integrated output noise E_O at 100 MHz: ~63 uVrms (G = 2) and ~166 uVrms (G = 7).

DERIVED, for the survey application (R_F = 1.5-2 kohm, C_D = 1 pF): Eq. 1 with GBWP = 2.7 GHz and C_TOT = 1 + 2.4 = 3.4 pF (no PCB parasitic) gives f-3dB = 290 MHz (1.5 kohm) and 251 MHz (2 kohm); the corresponding high-frequency noise gain (GBWP/crossover) is near the 7 V/V minimum stable gain, so the phase-margin data above (52 deg at 351 MHz, 7 V/V) are the relevant check.

Fig. 6-11 (p8): frequency response vs RF at G = 7: RF = 100 ohm gives no peaking but lower bandwidth, RF = 499 ohm peaks ~3.7 dB near 500 MHz; i.e. response depends on the feedback-node parasitic pole.
Fig. 6-6 (p7): noninverting small-signal response over temperature; bandwidth decreases at 85 C, peaking ~2 dB at -40 C.
Fig. 6-24/6-31/6-32/6-35 (p10, p12): VOS vs output current (15 units, ~+-0.5 mV over +-75 mA), VOS vs temperature (35 units), VOS histogram (centred ~0.2 mV), IOS vs temperature.
inconsistencies_and_uncertainties: PD pin polarity: pin table (p3) 'low = enable, high = disable' contradicts the EC table thresholds (p6) and Fig. 8-9 'Connect PD to VS+ to enable'.
Supply range: Sec. 8.3 says 6 V to 12 V (+-6 V); Recommended Operating Conditions and EC table give 13 V max; comparison table +-6.5 V; abs max 13.5 V.
Max junction temperature: Sec. 8.4.1.1 says do not exceed 105 C, abs max table says TJ 125 C.

Input bias current: EC table 4 pA typ / 25 pA max at 25 C (histogram Fig. 6-34 agrees), but the 25 C curve of Fig. 6-30 sits at ~25-30 pA (53 pA at VCM = -4.9 V); the plot conditions (self-heating) are not stated.

Current noise: EC table 3 fA/rtHz at 10 kHz vs ~2.5 fA/rtHz on the simulated curve (Fig. 6-20); 145 fA/rtHz at 1 MHz agrees with 142 on the curve. The curve is a simulation labelled 'Common-mode noise' with no stated definition.

Sec. 8.2.1.2 text: Eq. 3 is printed with C_EQ on the left-hand side; solving Eq. 2 for the tee capacitor gives C_T = (C1 C2 - (C1 + C2) C_EQ)/C_EQ. The text also says 'set C_EQ = C_TOT' where C_EQ = C_F = 0.092 pF is meant (C1 = C2 = 2.2 pF and C_EQ = 0.092 pF give C_T = 48 pF, matching the 47 pF used).

Sec. 8.2.2 text quotes the output noise as '64 nV/rtHz at 100 MHz' (G = 2) and '166 nV/rtHz' (G = 7); in Fig. 8-8 these numbers match the integrated output noise E_O in uVrms at 100 MHz (right axis), not the density e_O (5-8 and ~17 nV/rtHz).
Closed-loop bandwidth at G = 7: 765 MHz in the EC table vs 790 MHz in Sec. 7.3.3 text.
Open-loop gain: 92 dB typ (EC, dc) vs ~94 dB on the simulated Fig. 6-21 plateau.
Front-page TIA bandwidth plot carries no measured/simulated label; values coincide with Eq. 1 (calculation).
Package materials pages are dated 3-Sep-2026, later than the December 2025 revision date of the data sheet.
